cores.material: electrospun polyacrylonitrile/benzoxazine nanofibres cross-linked at 240 C, with 25 wt% SiO2 nanofibres (800 C calcined); freeze-shaped
cores.architecture: hierarchical cellular (open-cell, major and minor pores), isotropically bonded nanofibre network, negative Poisson ratio in compression
cores.density_as_printed: 9.6 mg cm-3 (Methods: "with a density of 9.6 mg cm-3"; Fig. 2 caption states the same)
cores.E_c_basis: tangent modulus (dσ/dε) in the Hookean/linear regime (ε<60%), compression; sample 9.6 mg/cm3

cores.sigma_c_as_printed: 10.6 kPa for the first elastic regime; 36.1 kPa at 80% strain
cores.sigma_c_basis: maximum stress in the first (elastic) regime, as printed; definition ambiguous. 36.1 kPa is stress at 80% strain
cores.notes: Cylinders ~28 mm diameter, 3% prestrain, strain rate 30 mm/min. Same sample also measured in shear (sandwich clamp, 4 mm thick, to 100% shear strain): elastic to ~40% shear strain, plateau 40-70%, max shear stress 8.82 kPa, yield shear strain 61%; shear tangent modulus is plotted (Fig. 2f) but no number is printed. Tension (Fig. 2h): Young's modulus 62 kPa, max yield value 4.33 kPa, brittle. Alternate numbers for the same 9.60 mg/cm3 sample in SI Table 1: E' = 40.3 kPa, "Max stress" = 32.4 kPa (columns not defined in the SI; likely a dynamic storage modulus and a max stress at an unstated strain). The 10.6 kPa "first elastic regime" figure is inconsistent with 30 kPa x 60% strain, so its definition is ambiguous. Silica nanofibres are part of the structure (25 wt%), so this is a polymer/ceramic fibre aerogel, not pure silica or carbon.
